title: Tuna with Balsamic, Garlic and Capers
summary: Small tuna steaks seared for a minute or two a side, with a quick, glossy balsamic, garlic and caper sauce. Dinner for one in 10 minutes.

steps.text: Pat the tuna dry with kitchen paper and season it all over with the salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over a high heat until shimmering.
Sear the tuna for {timer:90s} per side for medium-rare. For rare, give it {timer:1} per side; for medium, {timer:2}.
Lift the tuna onto a warm plate and let it rest.
Turn the heat down to medium, add the garlic and cook for {timer:30s}, until fragrant.
Pour in the balsamic vinegar and the honey, and add the capers if using. Simmer for {timer:1}, scraping up any browned bits.
Stir in the butter until the sauce turns glossy.
Spoon the sauce over the tuna, scatter over the parsley, if using, and serve with the lemon wedge.

tips: The inside should stay slightly pink: tuna turns dry if it is overcooked.
For a sharper sauce, use red wine vinegar instead of the balsamic, about three-quarters as much.
Serve it with baby potatoes, boiled or roasted, with rice, or with green vegetables such as broccoli, asparagus or green beans. It is especially good with roast potatoes or a crisp salad.
